Hi Jonas / Laura,

Quick note — our pilot with enterprise customers goes live in three weeks and we just validated a set of latency-sensitive inference pipelines. We need a committed pool of dedicated GPUs for the pilot window (3 weeks, ~50 concurrent inferencers, P100-equivalent sustained) and strong guarantees around preemption during the pilot. Our legal/procurement team is asking whether Redwood can: (1) provide a dedicated tranche isolated from best-effort bursts, or (2) if fully isolated capacity isn't available, put in writing what preemption behavior / credits would look like.

I attached the capacity worksheet with their initial traffic profiles. We are ready to sign a short SOW if we can lock the capacity and an SLA for the pilot. Please let me know what you can commit to today — this is time-sensitive.

Thanks,

On Fri, May 21, 2027 at 09:42 AM Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Emma — thanks for the details and the worksheet. Looping in capacity and CS to give a path forward.

Team — reviewed the worksheet. Short summary of feasible options and tradeoffs (attached: capacity-decision-tree-v1.md):

1) Hard-dedicated pool (isolated nodes) — Pros: no preemption, simplest SLA. Cons: requires reserve of ~8 x A40-equivalent nodes for the 3-week window; impacts committed capacity we already promised for two existing dedicated deals in the same AZ unless we re-home them. Lead time: 36-48 hours to stand up if node pool is available.

2) Soft-reserve (logical reservation + burst lanes) — Pros: faster, preserves utilization. Cons: can be preempted by higher-tier reserved traffic; we can contract minimum usable capacity with credits for any preemption events. Implementation: prefix KV cache seeding + batch isolation; lead time: 24 hours.

3) Preemptible tranche with credit schedule — Pros: highest utilization, easiest operationally. Cons: no hard guarantee; must define credit bands per minute of preemption and an allowed number of incidents.

Operational constraints: current reserved commitments mean that hard-dedicated is only possible if we accept migration risk for two mid-sized customers (re-home to other regions or time shifts). That requires leadership sign-off for an exception.

Recommendation: offer CloudBright a soft-reserve with a canary hard-dedicated window for the first 48 hours of the pilot (option 2 + temporary hard isolate) plus a credit schedule for any subsequent preemption. Commercially, I'd accept a short SOW with a small committed spend and a clause that allows us to migrate the hard pool after the pilot if needed.

Karthik
Director, Capacity Planning
Redwood Inference
